method.source: AlphaSense Expert Insights, authenticated user browser
method.query: (Orladeyo OR BioCryst OR Takhzyro OR KalVista) AND (commercial OR "sales force" OR "market access")
method.scope: All Dates; 15 results screened, four full transcripts read, selected by role and relevance. Search proximity/settings can omit relevant documents; no KalVista result in this query is not absence from library.
method.storage: Paraphrased notes only, no full licensed transcript reproduced.
method.validation: Original transcript and biography inspected beyond generated Smart Summary. No external operational corroboration completed this pass.

interviews.title: Former Vice President Is Bullish on BCRX's Orladeyo for the Prevention of Hereditary Angioedema Attacks Though PHVS' Deucrictibant Is a Strong Competitor
interviews.role: Former BioCryst VP; product design/commercialization responsibilities; field-sales or launch ownership not established
observations: First-oral benefit and improved-oral competitive threat; expert acknowledges limited PHVS familiarity and quick press-release review.
COVID made launch expectations uncertain; expert viewed execution favorably.
Expected switching to a materially better oral if covered; expressed limited brand loyalty.
interviews.limitations: Opinion, not observed switching rate. Cross-trial efficacy headlines are not superiority evidence; dated 2024.

interviews.title: Former Sr. Director Believes TAKHZYRO Is Well-Positioned in Terms of Market Access but That New Entrants in HAE Could Be a Threat
interviews.role: Former Takeda senior director, US rare-disease pricing/contracting and payer marketing; direct relevant access experience
observations: Incumbent contracts, share and payer reluctance to disrupt stable patients can protect Takhzyro.
Inadequate control or route preference can create switch opportunities. General 3–6 month payer-review estimate is not a PHVS-specific observed lag.
Convenience appeals to patients; payers need clinical/economic justification.
Cannot quantify switching back or explain clinical reasons; some impressions from public market research.
interviews.limitations: No contracts, rebate sizes or measured switching denominators supplied. Does not establish a numerical access haircut.

interviews.title: Former VP at BioCryst Pharmaceuticals Believes ORLADEYO Could Become a Market Leader in HAE Treatment
interviews.role: Former BioCryst regulatory-affairs SVP, 2007–April2021; not a commercial-field leader
observations: Described market research exploring oral interest among patients already satisfied on injectables.
Direct commercialization versus regional partnerships selected by market.
Discussed longstanding HAE advocacy relationships.
interviews.limitations: Regulatory role and historical expectations. Apparent approval-date/drug-name errors in transcript; do not reuse clinical/timeline claims. No quantified study results supplied.

interviews.title: Former Regional Manager Believes CSL.AU's Lackluster Market Access Capabilities Are Hurting the Company
interviews.role: Former CSL rare-disease regional manager; seven years including Haegarda and Kcentra; South Florida office-access experience discussed
observations: Described restricted provider access and hybrid virtual/in-person engagement.
Reported complicated hub processes, customer frustration and incomplete remediation. Believed service scope/resources mattered.
Described Takhzyro convenience/device advantages; Haegarda messaging emphasized efficacy/safety. Comparative superiority claims are unvalidated sales opinions.
Perceived weak coordination with contracting teams; considered streamlining access more useful than extra marketing.
Recalled competitor manufacturing disruption producing excess launch demand and a waitlist; timing/magnitude not independently verified.
Reported compensation/retention concerns; no turnover statistics.
interviews.limitations: Single former employee, mixed products and regional experience. Do not extrapolate Kcentra hospital-budget anecdotes to HAE. Hub causality, relative pricing and launch supply history need issuer/operational corroboration. Speculation on legal need for outsourcing excluded.

model_status: Qualitative mechanism evidence only; no numerical adoption assumptions changed.
